title: Which line of latitude is most land?
hook: Earth is mostly ocean. Is that true wherever you walk around it?

knows: that most of Earth's surface is ocean
doesNotKnow: that the share of land changes sharply with latitude
that most land lies in the northern hemisphere

misconception: Land and ocean are mixed in roughly the same proportion at every latitude.
objective: The learner can say that a walk around 65°N is mostly land (77% on the lesson's data) while a walk between 40°S and 60°S is almost all sea, so land is concentrated in the north.
keyState: 65°N and a parallel between 40°S and 60°S have both been visited, with the land share shown.

claims.text: On the lesson's map data, about 77% of a walk around 65°N is over land.
claims.source: parallels.json, generated by gen.mjs (committed alongside): 3,600 samples every 0.1° of longitude against the kit's Natural Earth 1:110m land polygon with d3 geoContains; 65°N share 0.7744. Matches the cm-geography brief (77.4%).

claims.text: 65°N crosses Russia, Canada, Alaska, Greenland, Iceland, Scandinavia and Finland.
claims.source: Builder scratch run: sampling 65°N every 0.1° against the kit's 1:110m countries: Russia 41.5%, Canada 18.9%, United States (Alaska) 7.2%, Greenland 3.3%, Iceland 2.6%, Sweden 2.1%, Finland 1.3%, Norway 0.7%. Stage wording says 'Scandinavia and Finland' because Finland is not usually counted in Scandinavia.

claims.text: On the lesson's data the equator is about 21% land and 40°N about 45% land.
Between 40°S and 60°S a walk around the world is almost all sea (60°S: none of it on land), until Antarctica fills the parallels near the South Pole.
claims.source: parallels.json: shares from 40°S to 65°S are at most 4.3% (41°S; Chile, Argentina, New Zealand), 0.0% from 56°S to 63°S; 70°S 38%, 75°S 70%, 80°S 75% (Antarctica). Antarctica's coast and ice shelves are simplified at 1:110m, so no southern figure beyond 65°S is quoted on the stage except as the readout.

claims.text: Most of Earth's land is in the northern hemisphere.
claims.source: Commonly quoted as about two-thirds of land area north of the equator (e.g. NOAA / standard physical geography texts; from memory, needs a source). The stage shows it parallel by parallel; not computed as an area share here.
About 71% of Earth's surface is water (USGS Water Science School, from memory). Kit data: land is 28.9% of the sphere by area (cm-geography brief).

claims.text: A parallel is a line of latitude.
claims.source: Definition (Snyder 1987, Map Projections: A Working Manual, glossary; from memory).

recall.question: Sailing once around the world along 50°S, how much of the route is over land?
recall.why: Between 40°S and 60°S the world is almost all ocean; most land sits in the north, where 65°N is about three-quarters land.
